mechanism:
Per ayah (ORCHESTRATION.md "Fixed Sequence"; README.md):
0) prepare (script workflow.py, deterministic). From bundles/sNNN/S_A.ayah.json it builds three hermetic prompts: micro, macro and global.discovery.prompt.md. Each holds an instruction template (prompts/discovery.md), the four pinned governing documents in full (guidance/PRINCIPLES.md, COMMENTARY_SPEC.md, CHANNELS.md, PROMPT_V2.md; 69,650 bytes), and a single-line lane packet JSON. Packet keys (my packet.py on 100:1 macro): branch_registry 387 KB (116 focus-root branch cards with gloss, semantic_detail, boundary, review_facets), support_registry 267 KB, candidate_inventory 70 KB, hft_evidence 55 KB, selected_context_units 53 KB, connection_registry 21 KB (inter-ayah rows; 150-250 rows in global), plus focus/QAC alignment. Candidate types (100:1): micro = word_topic, focus_root_occurrence and HFT baseline_model; macro = channel resonance_nomination (trusted) plus HFT context_delta and surprising_outlier (legacy_unbound); global = v12 cross-run published_finding, reader_walk and reader_summary_claim, hft_reader_extension. Prompt sizes (my sizes.py over 1,130 prompt sets): median micro 565 KB, macro 753 KB, global 892 KB, about 2.2 MB per ayah; max global 3.94 MB. 29:38 measured 848/997/1,370 KB (AUDIT); 22:5 global 7.4 MB (v6/README.md).
1) Three fresh scope agents, gpt-5.6-luna at max, run in parallel. Turn 1 (discovery) decides every candidate (accept, narrow, represented or reject, with reasons and branch/facet/context/obligation exclusions) and writes findings with claim, mechanism, reader_payoff, containment, epistemic status (grounded, qualified or exploratory), and branch_activations (branch_ref, facet, carrier_refs, trigger_refs, focus_return_refs, application_mode). Schema: commentary-v5-scope-discovery-v1.
2) Turn 2 of the same agent (prompts/composition.md) writes Turkish scope prose (*.scope.tr.md) and a landing ledger mapping every finding movement to a paragraph anchor. The agent runs validate_scope_ledger.py itself.
3) CE: one fresh gpt-5.6-sol max consolidator, prompts/canonical.md. Input = the three scope proses, the three ledgers, the four guidance docs and a focus brief; discovery JSON is deliberately excluded. Canonical prompt median 205 KB, max 996 KB. It writes S_A.prose.tr.md, then in the same session the editorial pass (prompts/editorial.md), validate_prose.py with up to 2 repair cycles, and a fixed "qualification/image presentation" follow-up with revalidation.
4) prepare-middle (script) renders a hermetic middle-layer prompt (median 44 KB). A fresh gpt-5.6-luna max agent writes lossless-compressed middle prose, then gets the fixed audit follow-up (prompts/middle-layer-audit-followup.md). The orchestrator must not inspect the output.
5) prepare-invitation renders the invitation prompt from the editorial (median 31 KB). A fresh Luna max agent writes a 2-4 paragraph selective reading invitation that follows one or two channels.
6) Optional continuation outside v5: _surah_commentary/v2 (editorial-v1) builds surah readings from the editorial texts only. 36 runs consumed v5 editorials (grep of source-packet.json).
Operations: a Firebase monitor (operations/monitor.py) records start and terminal events only; runtime state ends 2026-09-10 (operations/runtime/snapshot.json). Agents are launched with "the multiagent spawn tool, not codex exec" (ORCHESTRATION.md).
Stances: all three lanes are generative-plus-adjudicative in one prompt (accept/reject during discovery). CE is a "non-compression" merger ("every retained finding… must land explicitly"). The middle layer is lossless compression; the invitation is the only selective stage.

north_star_scorecard.evidence: Editorials open on the plain scene. 12:84: 'Böylece ayetin ilk zemini açıktır: kayıp karşısında yön değiştiren… bir baba' (editorial/s012-p05-with-fatiha/s012/12_84/12_84.prose.editorial.tr.md); 100:1 opens with the oath scene. But length and machinery work against orientation. Median 2,247 words (S1 Astra median 8,671; my words.py). Astra comparison: 'several openings sound like methodological notes'. The 09-04 review (#8) found production facts in reader prose ('target morphology or trust levels were not established').

No Turkish-loss worklist or instruction. PROMPT_V2.md only frames the reader ('Turkish loanwords that have shifted, narrowed, or lost their meaning') and grammar the reader cannot hear. The proxy 'Türkçe' appears in 4% of S5-32 editorials and 19% of S87-114 (my proxies.py). v13/DESIGN.md credits Turkish loss to v11/v12, not v5.

The macro lane gives median 10 findings per ayah; median 14-16 same-surah refs per editorial (proxies.py). 5:6 editorial links قُمْتُمْ to قَوَّامِينَ (5:8), but has no kaʿb→Kaʿba 'qiyāman' and no mirfaq-leaning reading (grep of editorial/s005-p01-with-fatiha/s005/5_6). The same branches recur across many ayat (S18: 329 branches activated in ≥5 ayat), so the resonance is often not focus-specific (my inference).

Network-v3 channel nominations enter macro as 'trusted' candidates (resonance_nomination), and HFT context deltas as legacy_unbound; they are accepted or narrowed, not rediscovered. But each ayah runs independently and in parallel ('Do not finish one ayah end to end before starting the next', ORCHESTRATION.md), so there is no progressive disclosure across ayat. The v11 comparison lists v5 S1 surah chains (A-F), with the caveat that those surah files are partly from an Aug 19 run (compare_s001_v5.md).

No concordance or recurring-role input. The standard 18:86 editorial cites none of 15:26/15:28/15:33, and 18:96 cites none of 15:29/38:72/3:49/5:110 (my grep). v10/DESIGN.md: 18:86 'the creation association is briefly named, but the clay passages are not used'. The exhaustive inter-ayah test did surface both patterns (18_86 inter-ayah prose: 15:26 ×2, 15:28 ×3, 55:14 ×3; 18_96 editorial: 15:29, 38:72, 3:49, 5:110, 21:91, 66:12, 32:9), but inside 71,476-word and 15,623-word catalogues.

The global lane exists, but QeQ is not sequenced after latent readings and the prose never labels supports/expands/shifts/contradicts. Luna/Sol editorials cite median 8 other-surah refs, 3.7% of pushed row targets (rows.py). v9/DESIGN.md: 'V5 global lane used 0 of 253 inter-ayah rows for 29:38'. The Astra S1 editorials are much broader (357 distinct refs). compare_s001_v5.md: 'v5 still wins on thematic cross-reference breadth, especially ethical and practical mercy verses and counter-verses'. All 86 non-S1 refs in 1:3 came from the pushed connection_registry (rows.py-style check).

v13/DESIGN.md: v5 gained 'dictionary breadth; most gold ingredients present' and lost '"refuses to assemble them"; catalogue feel'. The Astra comparison shows Luna discovery already held the creditor-advance, straying-as-lost-findability and water/well readings ('Luna is already supplying valuable discoveries'). compare_s001_v5.md lists v5's water system, womb→cultivation chain and flock belonging, which v11 dropped. The editorial is 'non-compression' (every finding must land), so it aggregates rather than integrates.

Discovery prunes and scores. Across 84,062 candidate decisions: 17,675 reject, 8,208 narrow, 4,358 represented. Global rejects 8,097 of 16,847 (48%), mostly for missing anchors or focus return ('unanchored summary', 'no exact carrier'). Every finding gets grounded/qualified/exploratory (30,643/28,627/4,788) (my disc.py). Benchmark: 'Luna treats registry=unresolved as a disqualification'. Astra comparison: 'an expensive editor… cannot legitimately recover rejected findings'.

A mandatory 'containment' field per finding, and composition requires the ordinary reading intact. But negatives are dense: 'değil' at 5.4 per 1,000 words in Luna/Sol editorials, 2.9 in Astra (proxies.py). Astra comparison: 'persistent defensive qualifications'. 100:1 editorial: 'bir hayvan adını değil, koşma eylemiyle tanınan… topluluğu getirir' (not-X-but-Y form).

Discovery JSON is fully anchored (branch_ref, facet, carrier_refs, trigger_refs, focus_return_refs; exact IDs). Prose carries ayah refs near each comment (a rule in editorial.md) and all Arabic in {ar,tr,gloss} tags: 942 of 942 editorials pass validate_prose.py (my run). But only 4 of 942 editorials name a classical dictionary, none uses source:S:A or source:root hover tags, and memory-only senses are not marked (the packet boundary replaces marking).

The hermetic packet boundary and per-candidate exclusion records hand exclusions forward inside the JSON. But CE never sees the JSON (ORCHESTRATION.md section 4). Astra comparison: the 1:5 editorial lost palm/rain, spring/delivery and the leaking container present in macro scope ('the clearest substantive retention regression'). The earlier Luna/Sol 1:5 smoking perfume vessel 'went beyond that evidence'. B009 delay/non-delay polarity is inconsistent across ayat. The kāna-predicate grammar error survived CE (review #6).

v5 is ayah-level by design ('Not "what does the surah argue" — that is layer 3's job', guidance/PROMPT_V2.md). The separate _surah_commentary/v2 editorial-v1 continuation produced 36 surah readings from v5 editorials only (S1, 5, 12, 17, 18, 19, 31, 32, 87-114; e.g. runs/editorial-v1/s100/.../100.surah-reading.prose.tr.md, 1,685 words). Not rated here beyond existence.

Cheap only because it is all Luna/Sol: S12 about $0.61/ayah for discovery plus composition at Luna rates, about $0.69/ayah whole-workflow projection (v8_batch/COSTS.md; v9/DESIGN.md:218). Volumes are huge: about 1.5M input tokens per ayah before CE, and 2.2 MB of discovery prompts per ayah. There is no funnel (composition re-reads discovery; CE re-reads three proses plus 69 KB of guidance), no Opus synthesis, no cached shared prefix, and Batch was built but never run. Pricing the same volumes at Astra gives $38.8/ayah (s001-astra-model-pricing-estimate.md). NORTH_STAR: 'Bulk evidence re-read by every step made v5 expensive'.

recorded_verdicts.verdict: "The defensible model conclusion is: this Astra-led run is analytically stronger overall, but not uniformly better edited, and one evolving run does not isolate the model effect from the new follow-up or normal run variation."

"Luna is already supplying valuable discoveries, not merely raw hints of the obvious meaning… an expensive editor can clarify weakly expressed retained findings; it cannot legitimately recover rejected findings, reverse explicit scope restrictions, or add missing evidence." Proposed test: "Luna max for the three discovery/scope sessions, Astra high for the existing consolidation/editorial session, and Luna max for invitations."

"v11 ≥ v5 on depth, precision and surah architecture. v5 still wins on thematic cross-reference breadth, especially ethical and practical mercy verses and counter-verses. A targeted 'concept concordance plus caveat' pass would close most of the gap." Also: "The v5 prose cites 357 distinct refs. v11 cites 426. 190 of v5's refs also appear in v11. 167 appear only in v5" and "The caveat verses are the most consequential gap."

"What v5 finds that v11 rightly drops. v5's HFT pipeline produces many material and embodied metaphors from marginal, sound-alike or split-root branches: water systems, rain cycles, womb-passage, gift/offering, covenant… Two are worth retrieving: Womb → cultivation (chain B)… 1:4 → 1:6 q-w-m." Note: NORTH_STAR lists the Fatiha water system (rain, gathered water, well and pulley) as a target 'aha', so this verdict conflicts with the North Star.

failure_modes: Pushed bulk not read or used. 29:38 global used 0/253 inter-ayah rows (v9/DESIGN.md). Luna/Sol editorials cite median 3.7% of pushed other-surah row targets (my rows.py, 120 ayat).
Registry metadata treated as a verdict: 'registry=unresolved' excluded HFT-traced branches (benchmark: Failed Stability 3/12 in the lexical-prose run).

Evidence-binding failure turned into semantic rejection: 8,097 global rejects, crudely 5,247 'no anchor/focus return' (my disc.py sample of reasons, e.g. 'The HFT payload is an unanchored summary with zero exact anchor refs'). Review #2: 'A failed evidence binding should be distinguishable from a semantic judgment'.
Lane misrouting: candidates rejected because the context was outside the lane (review #2, #3).
Loss of the explanatory chain between lexical source and image in CE (review #5), and outright retention loss (Astra comparison, 1:5).
Accounting prose from landing ledgers (100:1 macro scope 31,163 words of 'ilk temasta… ikinci temasta…').

Generic or templated activations. 18 discovery files contain the template trigger 'Independent contextual grounding enters at…' (e.g. 99:7 macro 117/191 activations, 87:2 98/211, 100:1 63/354; my disc.py). v6 V5-semantics pilot: 9 of 15 findings were generic placeholders.
Grammar error surviving all stages: mustabṣirīna called a transitive object instead of kāna's predicate (review #6).
Source-polarity inconsistency: root_000973/B009 'brief delay' versus 'non-delay' handled differently in 1:4, 1:5, 1:6 and 1:7 (Astra comparison #3).
Evidence overreach from association: a smoking incense vessel from a perfume-mortar branch (Astra comparison #4, earlier Luna/Sol 1:5).
Defensive negatives and machinery leaking into reader prose ('değil' 5.4 per 1,000 words; review #8).
Run-to-run selection variance: S1 1:6 macro 44 → 33 → 45 findings across reruns (Astra comparison); 29:38 Failed Stability 12/12 → 3/12 → 12/12 across arms (my git check).
Verbosity scales with the stronger model and the extra follow-up: 2.15x words (Astra comparison).
Invitation overlap across a surah: 1:1/1:3 gestation, 1:5/1:6 assisted walking (Astra comparison).

Operational: the monitor could synthesize 'passed' without a lifecycle event (review #10); stale bundles failed preparation (73:20, 14:22; review #9); the S13/S14 runs stopped after 3 ayat each (reason unknown).

Artifact wrinkles: S19:60-73 use alternate filenames (micro/macro/global.prose.tr.md and *.landing_ledger.json); 2 discovery files with nonstandard schema strings (18:47 macro 'v5.discovery.macro.1', 91:14 macro 'v5-macro-scope-discovery'); 5:12 global coverage_complete false; a stray output/s019-regular-20260912/s019/19_17/global.discovery.json.
dilution_evidence: Hurt: the Sept 4 packet expansion (routing, 330 obligations, context morphology +639 KB global, repeated records +341 KB) coincided with a user-reported behaviour regression and was rolled back (AUDIT_V5_INPUT_COMPATIBILITY_2026-09-08.md). The measured separate contributions were 'not experimentally isolated'.

Mixed: re-embedding the full 69 KB guidance in discovery 'recovered some macro imagery but did not consistently recover the earlier word-to-image explanations' (AUDIT). The full-guidance macro run had 12 findings but 28 distinct branches, against 7 findings and 39 branches in compact (my git check).

Hurt: pushed bulk was ignored. The 29:38 global lane used 0 of 253 rows (v9/DESIGN.md). Luna/Sol editorials used median 3.7% of about 181 pushed row targets (rows.py). Rows only reached prose when turned into a per-row worklist (inter-ayah test found the NS5 clay/breath patterns for 18:86/18:96 that the standard lanes missed).

Review #4 (commentary-v5-review-2026-09-04.md): 'The prompt payload is substantially larger than the discovery task needs' (branch registry about 580,000-621,000 characters per lane; the four governing documents about 10,600 words per lane; 'The Fatiha examples can also prime an interpretation'). It warns that one-line JSON can be truncated by bounded reads.

Hurt: more instructions and steps downstream. The presentation follow-up made the prose state each function twice ('principal reader-facing regression'), and length grew 2.15x without proportional value (Astra comparison: 'More explanation is not automatically more value for either the reader or the budget').
Hurt: the 'every finding must land' ledger produced catalogue or accounting prose (100:1 macro scope 31,163 words). v13/DESIGN.md: 'catalogue feel'.

Helped: small targeted additions. Reviewed 8.63 KiB supplements for 29:38 (tent frame, socket, upright support; 7:201/29:39 QAC) were approved as bounded evidence (AUDIT). Their effect was not measured.
Helped: one targeted instruction (legacy_unbound HFT traces count as attributed evidence) closed about 90% of the benchmark gap (benchmark; prompts/discovery.md).
luna_evidence: Good at discovery breadth. Astra comparison, 'What Luna Already Had': 1:4 creditor supplies the capacity to answer (macro:cand_f0238210878c5c01408d); 1:7 'Straying becomes a loss of recoverable orientation, so guidance appears as restoration of findability'; 1:2 water, well and continuous nurture; 1:6 supported procession. 'Paying for discovery again to obtain that same core is hard to justify from this evidence.'

Good at following schemas and worklists at scale: 2,844 discovery JSON all parse, 2,843 coverage_complete, 84,062 candidate decisions each with a reason, 96,140 activations with carrier/trigger/focus-return refs; ledgers validate (disc.py; 150/150 validate_scope_ledger.py). Benchmark: 'Epistemic calibration: appropriate grounded/qualified/exploratory labels'; 'All 4 channel candidates: accepted/narrowed with appropriate activations'.
Good at uncandidate discovery in the wider lanes: 1,948 findings with no origin candidate (global 1,165, macro 734, micro 49).
Bad: a registry label treated as disqualifying (benchmark). Fixable by instruction (NORTH_STAR: 'Luna's discovery gaps were instruction-fixable').
Bad: ignores pushed bulk rows (0/253 for 29:38) unless they are itemized as a worklist (v9/DESIGN.md lesson).

Bad: generic payoffs and templated activations in some files ('some Luna findings use a generic payoff such as perceiving the focus through a newly activated image', Astra comparison; 18 templated files). v6 V5-semantics pilot: 9 of 15 findings were generic placeholders.
Bad: run variance in what it accepts (1:6 macro 44/44/33; Failed Stability 12/12, 3/12, 12/12).

Bad at synthesis: NORTH_STAR says Luna 'does not synthesize'. v5's middle layer (Luna max, lossless compression of the editorial) has no recorded quality verdict in files. Its iteration commits on S1 1:5 cite 'exact-anchor and paragraph-density issues' (ce0a07fbb).
Sol (gpt-5.6-sol max) was chosen for CE after Luna/Sol/Terra cinematic arms on 29:38 (4f34d87ff, 4b2903dea); no written rationale. Sol/Luna editorials cite median 8 other-surah refs.

Astra (gpt-6-astra high, S1): 'analytically stronger overall', better at evidence roles and contextual counterexamples; stylistic gain is 'explanatory clarity, not brevity, warmth, or musicality'; 2.15x longer; estimated 45x Luna cost per ayah ($38.83 vs $0.86).
pretraining_vs_data_evidence: Pushed data made the difference for QeQ breadth. All 86 non-S1 refs in the Astra 1:3 editorial were present in the pushed global connection_registry (241 rows) (my check on input/s001-fresh-20260910/s001/1_3/global.discovery.prompt.md). The 'thematic concordance' credited to v5 in compare_s001_v5.md (3:159, 30:21, 42:28, 16:64, 17:82…) came from pushed inter-ayah rows, not memory. Whether a model used them depended on the model: Luna/Sol used median 3.7% of row targets, Astra 28% (rows.py).

Rare senses came from pushed dictionary branches. The eye-film sense of سبل (root_000672/B010, 'red-veined, web-like eye film') is in the packet; the benchmark calls it 'partly an Arabic knowledge test', and Luna retained it at reduced scope. The tent-frame, socket and upright-support branches (root_001222/B008 etc.) needed reviewed dictionary excerpts to be usable (AUDIT approved additions).

Benchmark: the Luna gap was 'NOT an Arabic knowledge gap (Luna identifies the 3 retained HFT branches correctly)'. It was an instruction-following issue, so pretraining sufficed once the instruction allowed it.

The dictionary as guard: the perfume-mortar branch root_000973/B012 'does not, by itself, supply burning incense'. The earlier prose's smoking vessel was a model association beyond the data, corrected when the run respected the branch (Astra comparison #4).
Pushed data can mislead: the short label of root_000973/B009 ('brief delay') contradicts its detailed scope ('non-delay'); models followed the label inconsistently (Astra comparison #3).
Grammar reasoning failed despite supportive data: word analysis described a copular construction, yet 'mustabṣirīna' became a transitive object and survived CE (review #6).

Specific concrete details depend on upstream acceptance, not model knowledge: Luna explicitly bounded 'No specific animal, retained afterbirth, or swelling specialization is asserted', while Astra used the retained-afterbirth image (Astra comparison). A downstream editor cannot add it legitimately.

NS5 recurring-role patterns (ḥamaʾ as human-creation clay; nafakha as animating) were not produced from pretraining in the standard lanes (18:86/18:96 editorials: 0 of the key refs). They appeared when the connection rows were processed one by one (inter-ayah test).

key_lessons: Q1: v5 left a large, well-formed and unused Luna discovery harvest: 909 ayat, 64K findings, 96K anchored branch activations, 84K decisions with reasons, all JSON-valid (disc.py). Recorded reviews agree the gold ingredients are mostly present ('most gold ingredients present', v13/DESIGN.md; 'Luna is already supplying valuable discoveries', Astra comparison). The failure was assembly, not discovery. Nothing has been re-synthesized from this harvest with Opus.

Q2a: in v5, pushed data, not memory, supplied the cross-references. 86/86 non-S1 refs in the Astra 1:3 editorial came from pushed inter-ayah rows, and rare senses (eye-film, tent frame) came from pushed branch cards. Pushed bulk was ignored by the cheaper pipeline (Luna/Sol cite 3.7% of row targets; 29:38 global 0/253). So the issue is attention and format (worklist versus background), not whether the data exists.

Q2b: labelled material in v5 is mostly model judgments, not gold. There is one Opus ideal catalog (29:38 macro, 42-43 activations), v5-only items reused as eval anchors (v11/eval/s001_anchors.md, v13/EVAL_ANCHORS.md), 70 semantic-unit ledgers and 161K finding-to-sentence alignments. They are sufficient for weak supervision or eval, not for training a distance model without human validation.

Q3: building on v5 is feasible if the new step (a) reads the discovery JSON (including rejects and narrows) rather than only prose, (b) uses a deterministic compact digest (median about 16 KB/ayah by my estimate) instead of 205 KB CE prompts, (c) drops the 'every finding must land' rule, and (d) uses Opus for integration. The recorded limit: 'an expensive editor… cannot legitimately recover rejected findings'. The harvest is also biased by early pruning and HFT relay (56% of activations are 'attributed'), and S1 is Astra-made.

Q4: v5's architecture splits by context distance (micro/macro/global), not by stance. Each lane holds generative and adjudicative stances at once (accept/reject plus epistemic labels during discovery), and a non-compression CE aggregates three proses, which yields a catalogue. A non-iterative alternative suggested by the evidence: script-built compact inputs, Luna per-item worklists only for recall (rows, branches), and one Opus synthesis that integrates, with no accounting ledger.

Q5: v5 never used a quran-slm distance. The same branches get activated for many ayat of a pericope (S18: 329 branches in ≥5 ayat). A useful distance should score focus-specific contact (branch × trigger word in the focus's window) rather than pericope co-presence, and could be evaluated on the 29:38 ideal catalog and the per-row inter-ayah ledgers.

Economics: v5 was cheap only because Luna and Sol did everything (S12 about $0.61/ayah for discovery plus composition at Luna rates). Its volumes (about 1.9M input tokens per ayah, estimated for S1) would be $15-39/ayah on Sol or Astra. The funnel, not the model, has to change for Opus synthesis.
Instruction beats volume for Luna: one targeted rule fixed about 90% of a recall gap (benchmark), while adding 700 KB of evidence or 69 KB of guidance did not reliably help (AUDIT).
